nice_guideline_used: CG126 / NG185 (Stable angina / IHD secondary prevention)

medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG185 recommends lifelong aspirin 75 mg for all patients with confirmed IHD

medications.purpose: Reduce LDL >40% and lower cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG185 recommends high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) for all IHD patients

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular and renal protection in T2DM with ASCVD
medications.nice_justification: NICE TA902/TA929 recommends SGLT2‑i for any T2DM patient with established CVD

medications.duration: Ongoing — BP and renal function review 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Blood pressure control, renal protection, and additional CV risk reduction
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG185 and NG136 list ACE‑I as first‑line for IHD and hypertension
NICE NG136 recommends CCB (amlodipine) as component of step‑3 therapy for hypertension

medications.duration: Ongoing — electrolytes and renal function review 6‑monthly
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends thiazide‑type diuretic as part of third‑line hypertension therapy

medications.dose: 500 mg extended‑release oral tablet once daily
medications.nice_justification: NICE diabetes guideline recommends metformin as first‑line therapy
Standard therapy for iron‑deficiency; not specific to NICE CV guideline but clinically indicated

interactions_checked.interaction: Ibuprofen can competitively inhibit aspirin’s antiplatelet effect if taken close together and increases renal risk when combined with ACE‑I.
interactions_checked.action: Advise patient to take ibuprofen at least 2 hours after aspirin or avoid regular ibuprofen; use paracetamol for routine analgesia.

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive diuretic effect may cause volume depletion, orthostatic hypotension, or electrolyte disturbances.
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure and weight after starting empagliflozin; consider reducing HCTZ dose if symptomatic hypotension occurs.

contraindications.reason: NSAIDs are contraindicated in patients with hypertension, diabetes, and ASCVD (NICE CG126/NG185; NG106) due to increased CV and renal risk.
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol (acetaminophen) for analgesia; limit ibuprofen to occasional PRN use with spacing from aspirin.

contraindications.reason: Negative inotrope; contraindicated in heart failure and can worsen ischemia (NICE CG126).
Negative inotrope; contraindicated in heart failure and may interact with beta‑blockers (NICE CG126).

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – NICE requires eGFR ≥45 mL/min/1.73 m² before starting empagliflozin and to adjust metformin dosing.
Liver function tests not provided – needed before initiating high‑intensity atorvastatin.
Allergy status to aspirin, statin, and ACE‑I unknown – verify no hypersensitivity before prescribing.
History of peptic ulcer disease or GI bleed not documented – assess risk before lifelong aspirin; consider PPI prophylaxis if high risk.
QRISK score not provided – not required for secondary prevention but would aid overall risk stratification.
treatment_summary: Add lifelong aspirin 75 mg, high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg, and empagliflozin 10 mg to the existing regimen of lisinopril, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, metformin, and iron. Avoid regular ibuprofen, monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, lipid profile, and blood pressure as per NICE CG126/NG185 and NG136. Provide patient education on timing of NSAID use, hydration, and signs of adverse effects.
